-3-  NC: 2025:KHC-K:7497-DB  MFA No. 200052 of 2023 HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant challenging by the judgment dated 11.04.2022 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-V, Vijayapura in MVC No.628/2020.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 01.05.2020, when the claimant was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-13- DA-6085 as a pillion rider along with Mallinath Dikshit as the rider near Nivaragi Village, on Umaraj-Nivaragi road, at that time, tractor bearing registration No.KA-28-TC- 3934 came from opposite side at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the vehicle of the claimant.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7497-DB HC-KAR 3.
The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.225,700/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the owner of the offending vehicle to deposit the NC:
2025:KHC-K:7497-DB HC-KAR compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.
Rohit S/O Pandurang Pattar @ Vedapatak @ ... vs Ogeppa S/O Madappa Dalwai And Anr

on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57564048/
3 6.
The learned counsel for the claimant has submitted that the claimant has sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
He has produced medical bills amounting to Rs.2,00,728/-.
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 21 days.
Even after discharge from the hospital, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment.

Considering the same,
the overall compensation granted by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

Secondly, he contended that in the connected matter in MFA No.201240/2023 filed by the claimants arising out of the same judgment and award of the Tribunal, this Court has fastened the liability on the Insurance Company and directed the Insurance Company to pay compensation to the claimants.
Hence, he sought to allow the appeal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7497-DB HC-KAR 7.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the claimant has sustained simple injuries and he has not examined the doctor regarding nature of injuries and disability suffered by him.
Some of the medical bills are duplicate.

Therefore,
considering the nature of injuries and medical records, the Tribunal has granted just and reasonable compensation and it does not call for interference.
Secondly, the learned counsel submits that he does not dispute the judgment passed in MFA No.201240/2023 in respect of liability is concerned.

Hence, he sought to dismissal the appeal.
8.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9. It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the accident occurred on 01.05.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7497-DB HC-KAR 10.
As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained cut lacerated wound over right side of left eye, over the lip, multiple abrasions over the fact, right shoulder.
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 21 days.
He has produced medical bills amounting to Rs.2,00,728/-.
He has not examined the doctor regarding nature of injuries and disability suffered by him.

Therefore, considering the evidence of the claimant, nature of injuries mentioned in the wound certificate and medical records,
we are inclined to award a compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- as against Rs.2,25,700/- awarded by the Tribunal.

11. In respect of liability is concerned, this Court in connected matter in MFA No.201240/2023 filed by the claimants arising out of the same judgment and award of the Tribunal, has directed the Insurance Company to pay compensation to the claimants with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, the Insurance Company is directed to pay compensation to NC: 2025:KHC-K:7497-DB HC-KAR the claimant in the present case also with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle 12.

In the result, the following order is passed:
Rohit S/O Pandurang Pattar @ Vedapatak @ ... vs Ogeppa S/O Madappa Dalwai And Anr on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57564048/
4
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- as against Rs.2,25,700/- awarded by the Tribunal.

d) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
The Insurance Company is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

Sd/-
(H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD) JUDGE Sd/-
